title: Unit normalization of the etale/pro-etale open-extension comparison
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion] and $A$ a finite discrete commutative ring. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Write $C_T=\nu_T^*$ and $R_T=\nu_{T,*}$ for the comparison adjunction, $e=j_!^{et}$ and $d=j_!^{pro}$ for the two extensions by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero], and $r=j_{et}^{-1}$ and $s=j_{pro}^{-1}$ for restriction. Let $\eta^e:1\to re$ and $\eta^d:1\to sd$ be their open-adjunction units. Let $a:C_Ur\xrightarrow{\sim}sC_X$ be the canonical inverse-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and $c:C_Xe\xrightarrow{\sim}dC_U$ the canonical comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison].

The sectionwise identification $rR_X\cong R_Us$ induces, by the comparison and open adjunctions, natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C_XeF,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,rR_XM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,R_UsM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(dC_UF,M).$$
These bijections send $h$ to $h\circ c_F^{-1}$. Moreover, for every etale $A$-module sheaf $F$ on $U$, the specified $c$ satisfies the unit normalization
$$s(c_F)\circ a_{eF}\circ C_U(\eta^e_F)=\eta^d_{C_UF}:C_UF\longrightarrow sdC_UF.$$
The comparison $a$ here is the canonical one above, not an independently chosen isomorphism.

proof.text: Use the existing canonical fixed-scalar open adjunctions and comparison adjunctions. The specified extension comparison is definitionally the inverse of the conjugate of the sectionwise identity theta. For any two adjunctions, the conjugation unit equation and naturality of theta identify the Hom chain with precomposition by the conjugate. Apply this to the composite adjunctions to obtain the asserted formula for every h.

Compute the conjugate of the specified restriction comparison a under C_X followed by s and r followed by C_U. Expand a into the inverse etale localization comparison, the specified inverse-image comparison, and the pro-etale localization comparison. Conjugation reverses composition and commutes with whiskering. Both localization comparisons are the canonical leftAdjointUniq maps and have identity conjugate. The remaining conjugate is exactly the canonical direct-image comparison delta by its definition.

Compute the mate of theta under the two restriction/direct-image adjunctions. On an etale object W over X, its section map is induced by the composite of the pullback of the first projection with the canonical pullback lift. This composite is the identity: apply pullback.hom_ext and use the two projection equations. Consequently the mate is delta, whose component is the identity on sections over the same chosen fibre product. The calculation is in ModuleCat and therefore retains scalar linearity.

Mathlib iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv identifies the twice-iterated mate with the conjugate. Steps 2 and 3 and injectivity of mateEquiv show that the comparison-adjunction mate of a is theta. Apply the same identity to the inverse extension comparison: its twice-iterated mate is theta by definition. Injectivity gives a as its open-adjunction mate. The unit_mateEquiv equation is C_U(eta_e) followed by a equals eta_d followed by s(c inverse). Compose with s(c) and cancel the inverse isomorphisms. This proves the second clause for every F, including the empty and zero cases.
